articles.title: Jake Gyllenhaal has joined a 10th annual US celebrity auction supporting custom homes for injured veterans; the charity has built more than 400 homes and bidding runs through November 20, 2026
articles.summary: Jake Gyllenhaal has joined the 10th annual Veterans Day Celebrity Auction hosted by Homes For Our Troops, the national nonprofit that builds specially
articles.body: Jake Gyllenhaal has joined the 10th annual Veterans Day Celebrity Auction hosted by Homes For Our Troops, the national nonprofit that builds specially adapted custom homes for severely injured post 9/11 veterans. According to the charity’s announcement and its Building Homes programme, the online auction opened on November 10 and will close on November 20, 2026, with every winning bid supporting homes designed to restore independence for injured veterans and their families.The auction is headlined by longtime supporters Jake Tapper and George Clooney, but its celebrity lineup extends well beyond them. Gyllenhaal appears alongside stars including Adam Sandler, Jennifer Aniston, Ben Stiller, Dave Chappelle, Jerry Seinfeld, Jon Bon Jovi, Paul Rudd, and Sarah Silverman, offering fans a chance to bid on experiences and memorabilia while supporting a practical cause. Read more details about it, as per the reports, here:What Gyllenhaal joinedGyllenhaal’s participation places him among dozens of entertainers, athletes, and public figures contributing to the milestone auction. The event gives supporters access to celebrity experiences, behind the scenes opportunities, meet and greets, and one of a kind collectibles.For bidders, the appeal is not only the chance to connect with a favourite star. Each winning bid helps fund Homes For Our Troops’ work building and donating mortgage free, specially adapted homes for veterans whose injuries make ordinary housing difficult to navigate. The organisation says its homes include more than 40 major adaptations, such as wider hallways and doorways, automatic door openers, generators, safe rooms, roll under sinks and counters, and pull down shelving. These features are intended to help veterans live more independently at home.A decade of celebrity supportThis year marks the 10th annual Veterans Day Celebrity Auction, a milestone for an event that has become a recurring part of the charity’s fundraising calendar. CNN anchor Jake Tapper, a national board ambassador for Homes For Our Troops, has helped organise and promote the auction for a decade. Tapper said the event matters because every bid and donation helps build homes that give severely injured veterans greater freedom and independence. His continued involvement has helped bring together celebrities, donors, and veterans around a cause that extends beyond a single fundraising night.George Clooney, another longtime supporter, returns as a headline host. He described the charity’s work as helping veterans and their families live more independently by creating homes adapted to the challenges they face.How the auction worksThe online auction is hosted through eBay for Charity at eBay.com/hfot. Bidding opened on November 10 at 4 p.m. Pacific Time, or 7 p.m. Eastern Time, and is scheduled to close on November 20 at the same time. The 10 day format gives supporters time to browse the offerings, place bids, and follow the competition. The auction includes a broad mix of experiences and collectibles, making it accessible to fans with different interests and budgets.Every dollar raised through winning bids supports the charity’s broader mission. Homes For Our Troops builds homes where veterans choose to live and continues its relationship with them after delivery, helping them rebuild their lives beyond the initial construction project.Why the homes matterHomes For Our Troops was founded in 2004 and has since built more than 400 specially adapted homes nationwide. The organisation says more than 90 veterans are currently on its active project list, with a long term goal of building a home for every veteran who qualifies for one.The homes are designed for veterans with severe injuries, including multiple limb amputations, partial or full paralysis, blindness, severe burns, and severe traumatic brain injury. By removing physical barriers and creating accessible living spaces, the charity aims to help veterans regain some of the independence they lost through service.The organisation says that a mortgage free, adapted home allows veterans to focus on recovery, family, education, and new careers. Many recipients have gone on to become advocates, speakers, and community leaders, using their experiences to raise awareness about veteran suicide, homelessness, and post traumatic stress disorder.A fundraising model with reachThe celebrity auction works because it turns fan enthusiasm into direct support for a tangible outcome. A bidder may be drawn by the chance to meet a star or own a collectible, but the money raised goes toward something practical: a home built around a veteran’s specific needs.Homes For Our Troops says nearly 90 cents of every dollar it spends goes directly to programme services supporting veterans. The charity is privately funded and relies heavily on individual donors and community fundraisers, alongside corporate and foundation support.The 10th anniversary auction also reflects how celebrity involvement can sustain attention for a cause over time. Rather than treating veteran support as a one time event, the charity has built a recurring tradition that brings new supporters into its work each year.What bidders can do nowWith bidding open through November 20, supporters have a limited window to participate. They can visit the auction page, review the available experiences and memorabilia, and place bids knowing that the proceeds support Homes For Our Troops’ home building mission.For those who cannot bid, the charity’s work continues beyond the auction. Its website outlines how donations support the construction of accessible homes and how the organisation works with veterans after they move in.Gyllenhaal’s involvement adds another familiar name to an effort that has already helped more than 400 veterans receive specially adapted homes. As the auction enters its final days, the focus remains on turning celebrity attention into lasting independence for the people the charity serves.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Operation Noor': Punjab cop's bullet-riddled body found, Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan claims responsibility; 5th killing since February
articles.summary: GURDASPUR: The killing of a Punjab Police head constable, whose bullet-riddled body was found on the roadside near Manakour bypass, has raised fresh
articles.body: GURDASPUR: The killing of a Punjab Police head constable, whose bullet-riddled body was found on the roadside near Manakour bypass, has raised fresh concerns over the safety of police personnel in the state's border districts. This is the fifth killing of a policeman in Punjab since February.Taking serious note of the incident, special director general of police (Law and Order) Parveen Kumar Sinha arrived in Gurdaspur on Monday to take stock of the situation and supervise the investigation. He also attended the cremation of head constable Vinod Kumar.Sinha and inspector general of police, Border Range, Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, shouldered the bier.Speaking to TOI, Sinha said preliminary indications suggested that it was a targeted attack on a policeman. “He died of a bullet injury. We are investigating all aspects of the case,” he said.Asked about the preliminary findings of the investigation, Sinha said the last available evidence with the police indicated that Vinod had taken a lift on a motorcycle from two persons whose faces were muffled. Investigators are examining the circumstances in which he came in contact with the two men and what happened thereafter.According to reports, Vinod, a wireless operator posted at Sujanpur police station in Pathankot, was a resident of Krishna Nagar in Gurdaspur. Following his promotion, he had gone to the Police Training Centre at Jahan Khelan and was subsequently sent to Sangrur for training. He was returning from Sangrur on November 15 when he was killed.Meanwhile, a CCTV footage shared by SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia on X purportedly shows two masked men abducting Vinod and shooting him. Majithia alleged that the head constable was kidnapped and murdered. The footage and the circumstances depicted in it have not been independently verified.“Guru Dokhi Bhagwant, criminals are openly shooting police personnel in the border areas. How are they operating with such impunity while you remain obsessed with 'tari wale baingan'? Is this your idea of law and order?”, he wrote.The killing has also reportedly been claimed by an outfit called Tariq-e-Taliban Hindustan in a social media post, which attributed the attack to its operatives under what it called “Operation Noor”. The post also threatened further attacks on security personnel. Police have not independently verified the claim.Sources said Vinod's body was found around 1 am after his family searched for him throughout the night. He is survived by his wife, two sons aged nine and five, and his 70-year-old mother.Chief minister Bhagwant Mann announced an ex-gratia grant of Rs 1 crore for the family, while HDFC Bank will provide insurance compensation of Rs 1 crore.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Amritsar | Silver Rate in Amritsar | Bank Holidays in Amritsar | Public Holidays in Amritsar | Petrol Price in Amritsar | Diesel Price in Amritsar | CNG Price in Amritsar | LPG Price in AmritsarStay updated with the latest Amritsar news. articles.title: Nukes, Iran, Ukraine and trade: Trump lays out agenda for trilateral with Xi, Putin
articles.summary: Three of the world's most powerful leaders are set to meet for the first-ever trilateral summit between the United States, China and Russia.
articles.body: Three of the world's most powerful leaders are set to meet for the first-ever trilateral summit between the United States, China and Russia.US President Donald Trump has outlined the agenda for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying the discussions will cover denuclearisation, Iran, the Ukraine war, economics and trade.Speaking to reporters, Trump said the three leaders would discuss denuclearisation, adding that the issue would be part of the agenda. "We're going to be talking about denuclearisation," he said, according to ANI.The proposed discussion comes after the expiry of the New START treaty between the US and Russia in February 2026. The agreement had placed limits on the strategic nuclear arsenals of the two countries. China has so far resisted joining nuclear arms control negotiations with Washington and Moscow.Iran is another issue Trump wants to raise during the meeting. "We'll talk about Iran," he said.Both China and Russia maintain strategic ties with Tehran. China is a major buyer of Iranian oil, while Russia has maintained military and diplomatic cooperation with Iran.The discussion could cover the ongoing conflict involving Iran and the role Beijing and Moscow could play in addressing regional tensions.Ukraine is another key issue Trump wants to discuss with Xi and Putin. Calling it his "favourite subject", Trump said, "Ukraine is losing. Ukraine and Russia are losing 25,000 souls per month, so we'll be talking about that."His remarks come amid continuing efforts to negotiate an end to the war. The inclusion of Ukraine is also notable as US officials had earlier indicated that the conflict would not be part of the trilateral discussions. Trump has now said he intends to raise the issue with both leaders.Trump also said economics and trade would feature in the discussions, without specifying the issues he intends to raise.The US and China continue to face trade disagreements over tariffs, technology and critical minerals. Russia's economic ties with China have also expanded since western sanctions were imposed on Moscow following its invasion of Ukraine.The trilateral meeting is scheduled for November 19 in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. It will bring together Trump, Xi and Putin for discussions on issues concerning international security, ongoing conflicts and economic relations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A California woman sold her $350,000 home after an AI scammer posing as ‘General Hospital’ star Steve Burton convinced her they were in love and would build a future together
articles.summary: A woman in Southern California lost her life savings and sold her home after becoming convinced that General Hospital actor Steve Burton was in love with
articles.body: A woman in Southern California lost her life savings and sold her home after becoming convinced that General Hospital actor Steve Burton was in love with her. The deception involved AI-generated videos and messages that made an impersonator appear and sound like the television star. According to ABC7 Chicago, the woman’s family discovered the scam only after substantial sums had disappeared. What began as an online conversation developed into a financial disaster, leaving her facing debt, possible bankruptcy and an uncertain future.How an AI romance scam using Steve Burton's identity beganThe victim, Abigail Ruvalcaba, began receiving messages on Facebook Messenger in October 2024 from someone claiming to be Steve Burton, the actor who portrays Jason Morgan on General Hospital. ABC7 Chicago said the impersonator sent videos that looked like Burton talking directly to Abigail and telling her he loved her.The videos were convincing enough to convince her she was talking to the real actor. AI had been used to recreate Burton’s look and voice, so it sounded as if the celebrity was speaking to her personally.The conversation eventually moved from Facebook Messenger to WhatsApp. According to Fox News, Abigail was encouraged to believe that the relationship was genuine and that the two could build a future together.The scammer reportedly discussed marriage and a shared life, making the relationship appear more personal than an ordinary exchange between a celebrity and a fan.The impersonator used money troubles to deepen the deceptionThe scam became more damaging when the impersonator claimed to have lost property during the Los Angeles wildfires. According to ABC7 Chicago, Abigail was told that Burton needed financial help and that the couple would eventually purchase a home together.The story gave the requests for money an apparent explanation. Instead of seeing the payments as suspicious, Abigail believed she was helping someone she loved through a difficult period.She sent at least $81,304 in gift cards, cash and Bitcoin, according to a Los Angeles Police Department incident report. The transfers drained her savings and left her in serious financial trouble.Fox News later described how the scam continued even after her available money had been exhausted. The impersonator encouraged Abigail to sell her condominium, presenting the decision as a way for them to begin a new life together.How did the scam lead to a home saleAbigail eventually sold her condominium in Harbor City, California, for $350,000. ABC7 Chicago reported that she had initially resisted the idea but later agreed after continued encouragement from the person she believed was Burton.The property sale represented a significant turning point. The condominium had been part of her family's financial security, but the impersonator persuaded her that selling it would help fulfil their supposed plans.According to Fox News, Abigail's daughter Vivian said the property was sold for considerably less than comparable homes in the neighbourhood. The quick transaction also meant that the family had little opportunity to intervene before the sale went through.The impersonator was expected to receive another $70,000 from the proceeds. However, Vivian discovered what was happening before that transfer could be completed and stopped it.KTLA reported that the family was left struggling to protect the property after the transaction. The condominium had subsequently been transferred to new owners, complicating efforts to recover it.Steve Burton confirmed the videos were fakeThe real Steve Burton was shown one of the videos used in the scam by ABC7 Chicago. The actor said the voice sounded exactly like his own, confirming why Abigail had struggled to recognise the deception.Burton also said that he knew of hundreds of people who had lost money to scammers pretending to be him. He said impostors often approached fans through comments on his verified Instagram account before directing them towards other profiles where money was requested.The actor made his position clear, saying he did not need fans' money and would never ask them for it. He also described meeting people at public appearances who believed they had maintained online relationships with him for years, only to discover that he did not know them.The family is fighting to recover the propertyAbigail's daughter Vivian stepped in after discovering the extent of the deception. According to ABC7 Chicago, she holds power of attorney for her mother and decided to speak publicly about the case to warn other families about the dangers of AI impersonation.The family has filed a lawsuit seeking to reverse the condominium sale. Their lawyer argues that Abigail was unable to distinguish between reality and the fabricated relationship, raising questions about whether she had the mental capacity to enter into the property contract.But the legal fight is being fought. The attorney for the buyers of the property told ABC7 Chicago that the claim that Abigail was unable to contract was not true and that the evidence was in their favor. It'll all be settled in court.The family hopes that sharing Abigail's story will make others more cautious about strangers claiming to be celebrities online.You use AI every day.
